newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican soap-opera star quits to kill her character.
newsitem.headline: Mexican soap-opera star quits to kill her character.

text.p: The sudden departure of the female star of Mexico's most controversial soap opera has left Mexicans up in arms and the television industry in turmoil.
Ana Colchero walked off the set of the hit show "Nothing Personal" just weeks before its cliffhanger ending, leaving the soap opera in the air and the TV Azteca network reeling.
Colchero said she deliberately quit to kill off her character, Camila, who began as a courageous and intelligent woman but later changed into a lying, irate patsy.
"It would be much better for Camila to disappear," she told Reuters in an interview on Friday at her colonial-style home in smart San Angel district of Mexico City.
"This was not the character agreed upon, and I had the moral obligation to put a stop to it."
"Nothing Personal" has been a ringing success for TV Azteca, an upstart network that has undermined the monopoly long enjoyed by media giant Televisa.
The show depicts the inner machinations of Mexico's corrupt political system in a way that the pro-government Televisa has never done.

Its plot revolves around the murder of an important laywer and reflects events that convulsed Mexico when Luis Donaldo Colosio, presidential candidate for the ruling party PRI, was assasinated in 1994. The PRI has ruled Mexico for 67 years.
Colchero said she was more concerned about the image of Mexican women on television in such a macho culture.
"My intention was to reflect Mexican women like myself, women who I believe we are," the actress said. She was surprised when her character became "a liar and a coward."
She said she was suing TV Azteca for breach of contract as it had changed her character's role without consulting her.
Colchero has come under attack not just for wrecking the show but also for her leftist politics.

One television programme attributed her departure to an alleged romance between the actress and Subcommander Marcos, the charismatic masked guerrilla who leads the Zapatista peasant uprising in southern Mexico.
Colchero laughed the report off as ridiculous. "The defamation has been a lot worse than I imagined," she said.
